R2-01.why: The Parent is the one character everyone watches every round, so Parent costumes, chaos finishers that everyone sees, and giftable Host House themes are purchases other players actually notice; a new house every month gives a steady flow of new things to sell. One rewarded video per session and R15 for adult DevEx add income without hurting play, but spending still depends on cosmetics alone, and kids, who are the majority of each lobby, get little to show off during the hunt.
R2-01.fix: Add kid-side items people see: caught/escape emotes and Report Card poses, plus a per-house 'trophy room' that shows each house's hotspot collection. Sell each new monthly house as a cosmetic bundle on launch day. Never sell priority for the Parent role.

R2-02.why: Under the Captain rule, a premium raft (bought or gifted) becomes the whole crew's experience, and a new vehicle every 2 weeks gives a regular product to sell. But seated avatars are small on screen, so personal cosmetics are barely seen, and only one buyer per crew gets value while friends ride free.
R2-02.fix: Add cosmetics for each seat that people see: paddle skins, splash and bonk effects, and seat emotes on the 'WHO SANK US?' card. Put each new vehicle in a bundle with its trail. Let crew members 'chip in' by gifting the host the vehicle.

R2-03.why: The disguise-pack design is fair and clever, but it is a paradox: in a hide-in-plain-sight game, a skin works as camouflage, so the buyer gets no credit or flex. What other players actually see is limited to prank effects when they are found and Guard costumes.
R2-03.fix: Give purchases a moment where they are credited: a post-round 'unmasking' that shows each statue's skin with the owner's name, and signature freeze poses or reveal stingers. Sell the Guard's flashlight beam colours and Guard tag effects as the item people notice.

R2-04.why: Ink trails and fusion VFX are seen by everyone on every cast, and fusions mix two players' cosmetics; this is the best visible cosmetic of any concept, similar to the skins and finishers RIVALS sells. But avatars stand still on balconies, a 4-player run has a small audience, and schools sold as shortcuts are a thin layer with no other repeat-purchase product.
R2-04.fix: Add boss-kill 'signature spell finishers' and rune-trail bundles each season that match the weekly mutator. Offer a capped 'second wind' tower revive through rewarded video, not a paid product. Make the Rune Book pages decoratable with cosmetic covers.

R2-05.why: Forger calling cards at the reveal are the MM2 lesson (cosmetics shown at the key dramatic moment), which is good, but tool skins are missing even though tools are on screen all the time. Visits to the personal museum will be low-traffic, so case and plaque sales will be weak.
R2-05.fix: Sell tool skins (magnifier, UV lamp, sniffer-dog breeds) shown full-screen during every inspection, and vote/accuse emotes plus reveal-punchline effects. Show a featured museum case in the shared lobby so museum purchases are seen.

R2-06.why: Dark horror, a Watcher sitting at a desk and dim corridors all limit who sees cosmetics, and the main lever (lobby decor) only shows between nights. The revive product sits near pay-to-progress in the most crowded genre, and Plus's free private servers eat into what friend horror groups would pay.
R2-06.fix: Sell cosmetics that show up in the dark: flashlight beam colours, CCTV filter and overlay skins the Watcher's whole team sees through pings, and ping/marker styles. Keep revives to rewarded video only, at most once per night, with no paid option.

R2-07.why: Every player's avatar is the star of the replay theatre that the whole lobby watches, so outfits and channel branding get a real showcase moment. Camera gear is earned and nothing else is for sale, so the catalogue is thin and has nothing that repeats.
R2-07.fix: Sell scream/flail/ragdoll animation packs and death-drag effects (funny, and they show in the replay), plus comment-screen themes and ghost 'cameo' skins. Run a seasonal cosmetic pass tied to the sponsor contracts.

R2-08.why: Parcel wraps are visible the whole time a parcel is carried, but the customer reactions people would pay for only fire on perfect deliveries, which a buyer rarely gets. HQ decoration is low-traffic, and uniforms are the standard default; this is a typical co-op cosmetic shop.
R2-08.fix: Have customer reactions fire on every delivery, scaled by value, and add van liveries under the Captain rule plus carry/wobble emotes. In Versus, sell cosmetic sabotage props (the banana peel's skin) that the other team sees.

R2-09.why: Creature collection is Roblox's strongest spending genre, and this has many items to sell (accessories for each critter, lineage banners shown to 3 opponents every match), convenience (nest slots), gifting, and a battle pass on a ranked season, all without selling randomness. The main risk is that critters affect power, so nest slots can read as pay-to-progress and draw FTC and algorithm scrutiny.
R2-09.fix: Normalize stats in ranked (by level band or a stat cap) so buying more nest slots gives more variety, not more power. Never sell hatch timers or speed-ups. Lean on giftable cosmetic critter accessories and visible lineage banners as the main revenue.

R2-10.why: With 2-player lobbies, any purchase is seen by one partner at most, and puzzle games have low repeat-spend intent. Device skins and sticker art packs are the only items, and there is no collection or convenience layer.
R2-10.fix: Add a collection meta, such as a 'blast album' of failure animations and cosmetic device trophies for each module type. Sell blast-effect packs and a cosmetic season pass. Offer daily-puzzle hints through rewarded video only.

R2-11.why: Vehicle liveries under the Captain rule and earnable vehicle shortcuts follow the Paddle Panic pattern, but there are only four big vehicles and a slower content cadence. Players run between stations in plain view, yet their tool and station cosmetics are not used.
R2-11.fix: Sell extinguisher-foam colours, patch-kit styles and crash-landing effects (shown in the slow-mo crash) that the whole crew sees. Release vehicles more often as smaller variants with livery bundles.

R2-12.why: Rainbow-water hose effects are on screen all the time, and 120 collectible critters give a large accessory catalogue, so this has the pet-sim appeal without selling eggs; truck liveries under the Captain rule, sanctuary expansions and a pass add to it. Revenue tied to the sanctuary depends on visits, which usually run low, and leaving rare critters unsellable caps upside, though that is the right call.
R2-12.fix: Show each player's top sanctuary critter (with accessories) riding the truck during runs, and allow giftable critter accessories. Bring a sanctuary 'tour' into the shared lobby so decor purchases are seen.

overall_notes: Calibration: median ARPPU is about $0.70 with about 3.8% of players paying, so games that sell only cosmetics with low visibility land at 4-5. Scores go up only where a purchase is (a) seen often by many players, (b) shown at a peak moment, or (c) tied to collection, convenience or gifting. Creature collection (R2-09, R2-12) and lobby-wide visible purchases (R2-01, under the Captain rule) lead. The Captain rule is a good social-purchase pattern, but each lobby has only one buyer, so pair it with personal cosmetics. Plus's free private servers lower private-server revenue for friend-group games (R2-06, R2-10, R2-02). R15 for adult DevEx (+42%) is listed only for R2-01 and should be the default everywhere it fits the art style. Watch pay-to-progress: R2-09 nest slots and R2-06 paid revive are the items most exposed to the FTC complaint and to scrutiny under the retention algorithm.
